summary:
A smart recycling bin system developed by students from SMK Sacred Heart for a Toyota Eco Youth competition could be expanded across markets in Sarawak under support from local councils, according to Bukit Assek assemblyman Joseph Chieng. The initiative aims to encourage greater public participation in recycling efforts and was praised by the state's Premier during its initial presentation.

Chieng hopes to promote the system further with backing from the Sibu Municipal Council and even other councils across Sarawak, emphasizing the potential for nurturing young talent and innovation in sustainability practices.

title: Sarawak ranks third nationwide in National Robotics Competition 2026 participation
excerpt: SIBU (July 31): Sarawak recorded its highest-ever participation in the National Robotics Competition (NRC) 2026, with 256 teams competing this…
stem_reason: The title and excerpt clearly indicate a robotics competition involving schools, which is a STEM-related event.
summary:
Sarawak participated with 256 teams in the National Robotics Competition (NRC) 2026, marking its highest-ever participation and placing third nationwide. The increase was due to a collaborative effort between the Sarawak Education Department and the Ministry of Education, which introduced structured training and expanded LEGO robotics sets to more schools.

This growth highlights Sarawak's strong performance in robotics, with past successes including 10 national championships and contributions to Malaysia’s overall World Robot Olympiad victory. The state aims to host the World Robot Olympiad 2027 and continues to emphasize STEM education through initiatives like the STEM Icon Sarawak program.

summary:
Eighty artificial reef balls were deployed off Kuala Nyalau to restore marine habitats, deter illegal fishing, and support local fishing communities. The project, a collaboration between Pembinaan Tukun Bebola (Sarawak) Sdn Bhd, Sarawak Forestry Corporation, and Bintulu Port Holdings Berhad, aims to enhance fish populations and conserve marine resources in Sarawak's waters.

Since 2022, PTBSB has contributed 467 reef ball units in Sarawak to promote sustainable fisheries and protect the state’s marine ecosystems.
